A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite figure relocation and the expansion of Appendix C.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic-data and image-classification experiments, transfer-learning results in Figure 13, and weight-spectrum experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds original SST-5 experiments and feature analyses of a pretrained VGG11 model on ImageNet in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The DLN formulation, losses, feature metrics, gradient-descent procedure, and projection-head approach are unchanged. Pretrained VGG11 is an additional subject of evaluation, not a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds SST-5 text classification and ImageNet evaluation to the retained synthetic, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR experiments. This substantially broadens coverage through a new data modality and a large-scale image benchmark.

E2.justification: Existing architectural comparisons are retained. SST-5 repeats the fully nonlinear MLP versus hybrid-network comparison, while VGG11 is analyzed independently rather than introduced as a competing baseline.

E3.justification: The new ImageNet experiment analyzes a PyTorch-pretrained VGG11 through feature extraction at eight specified layers. SST-5 explicitly reuses the Figure 1 settings except for the dataset; existing experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 extends checks of whether deep linear layers reproduce nonlinear feature behavior to SST-5 and adds a layerwise representation case study on pretrained VGG11. Existing depth, width, initialization, and projection-head analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed depth experiments, ten-run assumption checks, and three-seed transfer experiments with standard-deviation shading. The added experiments introduce no explicit run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes.

E6.justification: Figures 15–17 add SST-5 rank and training-accuracy curves and SST-5/ImageNet compression and discrimination curves. These provide additional instances of the retained trends under new settings; results in Figures 1–14 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumptions 1–2, theorems, Proposition 1, and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Discussion of weaker conditions attributes them to follow-up work rather than modifying this paper's formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims about layerwise compression and discrimination, nonlinear-network relevance, and transfer learning. The new experiments support existing claims without redefining the principal contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly frames Assumption 2 as relaxable and discusses follow-up results under weaker conditions; one nonlinear-rate sentence drops 'approximately'. Appendix C.2 interprets the new evidence as extending applicability to language and large-scale images.

D1.justification: V3 identifies the PyTorch-pretrained VGG11 source and extraction layers 2, 5, 7, 10, 12, 15, 17, and 20, and states that SST-5 reuses the earlier setup. Dataset-specific text encoding and ImageNet sampling remain unspecified; existing code and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of five neural-collapse follow-up works, including JSWM25's relationship to Assumption 2, plus SST-5 and ImageNet dataset citations. This is a focused update within the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording edits, adds short contextual discussions and an experimental cross-reference, and divides Appendix C into Assumption Discussion and Exploration on Other Datasets. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 15–17 and relocates several existing figures as the text reflows. Figures 1–14 retain their plots and captions, with no substantial redesign of the presentation.

improvement.justification: The SST-5 and ImageNet analyses broaden empirical support beyond v2's synthetic and smaller image datasets, while the follow-up discussion clarifies the assumptions' relationship to later research. The gain is limited: formal guarantees remain unchanged, and sparse preprocessing and sampling details constrain reproducibility of the added evidence.
